verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。）诸天述说　神的荣耀；穹苍传扬他的手段。
verses.en: For the music director, a psalm of David.The heavens declare the glory of God;[NOTE:1] the sky displays his handiwork.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 19. The psalmist praises God for his self-revelation in the heavens and in the Mosaic law. The psalmist concludes with a prayer, asking the Lord to keep him from sinning and to approve of his thoughts and words.
God’s glory refers here to his royal majesty and power.

verses.zh: 这日到那日发出言语；这夜到那夜传出知识。
verses.en: Day after day it speaks out;[NOTE:1] night after night it reveals his greatness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the work of his hands the sky declares.” The participles emphasize the ongoing testimony of the heavens/sky.

Heb “it gushes forth a word.” The “sky” (see v. 1b) is the subject of the verb. Though not literally speaking (see v. 3), it clearly reveals God’s royal majesty. The sun’s splendor and its movement across the sky is in view (see vv. 4-6).

verses.zh: 无言无语，也无声音可听。
verses.en: There is no actual speech or word,nor is its[NOTE:1] voice literally heard.
notes: Heb “it [i.e., the sky] declares knowledge,” i.e., knowledge about God’s royal majesty and power (see v. 1). This apparently refers to the splendor and movements of the stars. The imperfect verbal forms in v. 2, like the participles in the preceding verse, combine with the temporal phrases (“day after day” and “night after night”) to emphasize the ongoing testimony of the sky.

verses.zh: 它的量带通遍天下，它的言语传到地极。　神在其间为太阳安设帐幕；
verses.en: Yet its voice[NOTE:1] echoes[NOTE:2] throughout the earth;its[NOTE:3] words carry[NOTE:4] to the distant horizon.[NOTE:5] In the sky[NOTE:6] he has pitched a tent for the sun.[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “their.” The antecedent of the plural pronoun is “heavens” (v. 1).

The MT reads, “their measuring line” (קוּם, qum). The noun קַו (qav, “measuring line”) makes no sense in this context. The reading קוֹלָם (qolam, “their voice”) which is supported by the LXX, is preferable.
Heb “goes out,” or “proceeds forth.”
Heb “their” (see the note on the word “its” in v. 3).
The verb is supplied in the translation. The Hebrew text has no verb; יָצָא (yatsaʾ, “goes out”) is understood by ellipsis.
Heb “to the end of the world.”
Heb “in them” (i.e., the heavens).

verses.zh: 太阳如同新郎出洞房，又如勇士欢然奔路。
verses.en: Like a bridegroom it emerges[NOTE:1] from its chamber;[NOTE:2] like a strong man it enjoys[NOTE:3] running its course.[NOTE:4]
notes: He has pitched a tent for the sun. The personified sun emerges from this “tent” in order to make its daytime journey across the sky. So the “tent” must refer metaphorically to the place where the sun goes to rest during the night.
The participle expresses the repeated or regular nature of the action.

The Hebrew noun חֻפָּה (khufah, “chamber”) occurs elsewhere only in Isa 4:5 and Joel 2:16 (where it refers to the bedroom of a bride and groom).sn Like a bridegroom. The metaphor likens the sun to a bridegroom who rejoices on his wedding night.
The imperfect verbal form draws attention to the regularity of the action.

verses.zh: 它从天这边出来，绕到天那边，没有一物被隐藏不得它的热气。
verses.en: It emerges from the distant horizon,[NOTE:1] and goes from one end of the sky to the other;[NOTE:2] nothing can escape[NOTE:3] its heat.
notes: Heb “[on] a path.”sn Like a strong man. The metaphorical language reflects the brilliance of the sunrise, which attests to the sun’s vigor.
Heb “from the end of the heavens [is] its going forth.”
Heb “and its circuit [is] to their ends.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的律法全备，能苏醒人心；耶和华的法度确定，能使愚人有智慧。
verses.en: The law of the Lord is perfectand preserves one’s life.[NOTE:1] The rules set down by the Lord[NOTE:2] are reliable[NOTE:3] and impart wisdom to the inexperienced.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “is hidden from.”

Heb “[it] restores life.” Elsewhere the Hiphil of שׁוּב (shuv, “return”) when used with נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “life”) as object, means to “rescue or preserve one’s life” (Job 33:30; Ps 35:17) or to “revive one’s strength” (emotionally or physically; cf. Ruth 4:15; Lam 1:11, 16, 19). Here the point seems to be that the law preserves the life of the one who studies it by making known God’s will. Those who know God’s will know how to please him and can avoid offending him. See v. 11a.
Traditionally, “the testimony of the Lord.” The noun עֵדוּת (ʿedut) refers here to the demands of God’s covenant law.
God’s covenant contains a clear, reliable witness to his moral character and demands.

verses.zh: 耶和华的训词正直，能快活人的心；耶和华的命令清洁，能明亮人的眼目。
verses.en: The Lord’s precepts are fair[NOTE:1] and make one joyful.[NOTE:2] The Lord’s commands[NOTE:3] are pure[NOTE:4] and give insight for life.[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “the [morally] naive,” that is, the one who is young and still in the process of learning right from wrong and distinguishing wisdom from folly.
Or “just.” Perhaps the idea is that they impart a knowledge of what is just and right.

Heb “[they] make happy [the] heart.” Perhaps the point is that they bring a sense of joyful satisfaction to the one who knows and keeps them, for those who obey God’s law are richly rewarded. See v. 11b.
Heb “command.” The singular here refers to the law as a whole.
Because they reflect God’s character, his commands provide a code of moral and ethical purity.

verses.zh: 耶和华的道理洁净，存到永远；耶和华的典章真实，全然公义―
verses.en: The commands to fear the Lord are right[NOTE:1] and endure forever.[NOTE:2] The judgments given by the Lord are trustworthyand absolutely just.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb [they] enlighten [the] eyes.

Heb “the fear of the Lord is clean.” The phrase “fear of the Lord” probably refers here to the law, which teaches one how to demonstrate proper reverence for the Lord. See Ps 111:10 for another possible use of the phrase in this sense.
Heb “[it] stands permanently.”

verses.zh: 都比金子可羡慕，且比极多的精金可羡慕；比蜜甘甜，且比蜂房下滴的蜜甘甜。
verses.en: They are of greater value[NOTE:1] than gold,than even a great amount of pure gold;they bring greater delight[NOTE:2] than honey,than even the sweetest honey from a honeycomb.
notes: Trustworthy and absolutely just. The Lord’s commands accurately reflect God’s moral will for his people and are an expression of his just character.
Heb “more desirable.”

verses.zh: 况且你的仆人因此受警戒，守着这些便有大赏。
verses.en: Yes, your servant finds moral guidance there;[NOTE:1] those who obey them receive a rich reward.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “are sweeter.” God’s law is “sweet’ in the sense that, when obeyed, it brings a great reward (see v. 11b).
Heb “moreover your servant is warned by them.”

verses.zh: 谁能知道自己的错失呢？愿你赦免我隐而未现的过错。
verses.en: Who can know all his errors?[NOTE:1] Please do not punish me for sins I am unaware of.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the keeping of them [there is] a great reward.”

Heb “Errors who can discern?” This rhetorical question makes the point that perfect moral discernment is impossible to achieve. Consequently it is inevitable that even those with good intentions will sin on occasion.

verses.zh: 求你拦阻仆人不犯任意妄为的罪，不容这罪辖制我，我便完全，免犯大罪。
verses.en: Moreover, keep me from committing flagrant sins;[NOTE:1] do not allow such sins to control me.[NOTE:2] Then I will be blamelessand innocent of blatant[NOTE:3] rebellion.
notes: Heb “declare me innocent from hidden [things],” i.e., sins. In this context (see the preceding line) “hidden” sins are not sins committed in secret, but sins which are not recognized as such by the psalmist.
Or “presumptuous sins.”
Heb “let them not rule over me.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―我的磐石，我的救赎主啊，愿我口中的言语、心里的意念在你面前蒙悦纳。
verses.en: May my words and my thoughtsbe acceptable in your sight,[NOTE:1] O Lord, my sheltering rock[NOTE:2] and my redeemer.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “great.”

Heb “may the words of my mouth and the thought of my heart be acceptable before you.” The prefixed verbal form at the beginning of the verse is understood as a jussive of prayer. Another option is to translate the form as an imperfect continuing the thought of v. 14b: “[Then] the words of my mouth and the thought of my heart will be acceptable before you.”
Heb “my rocky cliff,” which is a metaphor for protection; thus the translation “sheltering rock.”
